subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated `before_persistence_write` hook for durable state changes, or represent durable-write policy through enriched `before_tool_call` and provenance contracts instead?
rationale: This choice defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what plugins can see, whether writes can be blocked or mutated, and how failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow additive hook with redacted targets, explicit block or mutation rules, bounded failure policy, docs, and coverage across representative writer paths.

options.title: Fold durable context into existing hooks
options.body: Extend `before_tool_call` and related provenance APIs instead of adding a hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to persistent-state provenance design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of the broader provenance/read-time trust model before implementing a write-only seam.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow additive hook with redacted targets, explicit block or mutation rules, bounded failure policy, docs, and coverage across representative writer paths.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest hook contract history and owns adjacent operator-policy security work referenced by this issue.
